title: Multimodal Management of Pediatric Choroidal Plexus Carcinomas: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study and Prognostic Factor Analysis
content: Background/Objectives: Choroidal plexus carcinomas (CPCs) are rare and aggressive pediatric tumors whose management is based on a multimodal strategy. Due to their very low incidence, the current state of science and prognostic data are mainly based on ret-rospective institutional series. Methods: This is a retrospective single-center cohort study comprehensively including all pediatric patients treated for choroid plexus carcinoma at the Lille University Hospital between 1991 and 2018. Clinical, surgical, histological and evolutionary data were an-alysed longitudinally. Results: 14 patients were included. The median age at diagnosis was 29 months, and 35.7% of patients had metastases at diagnosis. Complete surgical excision was achieved in 50% of patients. Estimated overall survival was 64.3% at 2 years and 57.1% at 5 years. Patients who underwent complete excision had a higher probability of survival than those who underwent incomplete resection. Exploratory analyses also suggested less favourable survival in patients younger than 2 years of age and in those with metastases at diagnosis. Conclusions: Pediatric CPC remains a tumor with a guarded prognosis. In this institu-tional cohort spanning nearly 3 decades, the extent of surgical excision appears to be the main factor associated with survival, highlighting the central role of surgery in the multimodal therapeutic strategy.
